inline_visuals.prompt: Clean technical diagram explaining PWM with three aligned rectangular command waveforms over equal time windows: 20 percent duty cycle, 50 percent duty cycle, and 80 percent duty cycle. Use consistent voltage axes, distinct ON and OFF regions, and simple visual labels. Show that the pulse height remains the same while the ON duration changes. Distinguish the controller command waveform from an actual motor-terminal voltage, which depends on driver topology and PWM mode. Premium robotics textbook diagram, white background, restrained blue and orange palette, technically accurate, minimal essential text.
inline_visuals.caption: The pulse height stays the same; duty cycle changes the fraction of time the command is in its on state.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Three aligned PWM command waveforms with identical amplitudes and different duty cycles of 20, 50, and 80 percent.

inline_visuals.caption: In the idealized example, a 40 percent duty cycle at 50 hertz means 8 milliseconds in the on state during every 20 millisecond period; 3.6 volts is only the assumed waveform average.
